findings.checklist_item: Specify per-surface invocation shape rather than a uniform `--output json`: `search` must be invoked WITHOUT `--output json` (it emits JSON by default and rejects the flag with exit 2); reserve `--output json` for show/list/ready; and confirm each parameter case actually reaches exit 0 on the fixed tree so the JSON-parse assertion runs for every surface.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine_support/reads_cli.py:483-494 — `_cmd_search` `elif arg.startswith('-'): print("unknown option") ... return 2` with no `parse_output` call
src/rebar/_engine_support/reads_cli.py:520 — search always `print(json.dumps(results...))` i.e. JSON is the DEFAULT, no flag needed
src/rebar/_engine_support/output.py:50-54 — `reader`/`ready` profiles accept json (show/list/ready), but search is not routed through parse_output
Plan quote: 'exit 0 implies stdout parses as JSON ... A LOUD nonzero exit is acceptable' — makes search's exit-2 pass vacuously
findings.finding: The plan's 'Run every surface with --output json' instruction is incorrect for the `search` surface: `_cmd_search` never parses `--output` and rejects any unrecognized dashed arg with exit 2, so `rebar search <query> --output json` returns a nonzero exit — which the plan's own invariant classifies as an acceptable loud failure. The search surface's output-integrity assertion would therefore NEVER execute (it passes hollowly on every run, including the RED reverted-ledge tree), defeating the generic property for a named target surface. search emits JSON by DEFAULT (no flag), unlike show/list/ready which accept `--output json`.
findings.location: Approach section: 'Run every surface with `--output json`'; Acceptance Criteria line 1 & 2
scenarios: Parameterized test runs `rebar search <q> --output json` -> exit 2 -> classified loud-OK -> JSON-parse assertion skipped -> search never tested, even under the reverted ledge (RED demo shows no search failure)
findings.suggested_fix: Parameterize each surface with its own arg tuple and expected shape, e.g. show=(['show', tid], object), list=(['list','--output','json'], list), ready=(['ready','--output','json'], list), search=(['search', <query>], list) — note search takes NO --output flag. Add an assertion (or design the RED demo) that each surface produces at least one exit-0 invocation so a rejected-flag exit-2 can't hollowly pass.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the search invocation: `rebar search` takes no `--output` flag (it always emits a JSON array), so invoke it WITHOUT `--output json` (bare `rebar search <query>`) and still assert exit-0 → parseable JSON array; do not let search's exit-2-on-unknown-flag pass vacuously under the 'nonzero exits pass' rule.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine_support/reads_cli.py:466-521 `_cmd_search` — no `parse_output`/`--output` handling; `arg.startswith('-')` → usage error `return 2` (line 483,494); unconditional `print(json.dumps(results...))` `return 0` (line 520) is the ONLY success path and takes no flag
src/rebar/_cli/help/overview.txt:36 — 'search  Full-text search over titles/descriptions/comments/tags (JSON)' — output is fixed JSON, not flag-controlled
Contrast: show/list use `parse_output(argv,'reader')` (reads_cli.py:107,212) and ready uses `'ready'` (reads_cli.py:412), all of which accept `json` — only search differs
MATCH/MISMATCH verdict: show/list/ready `--output json` = MATCH; search `--output json` = MISMATCH (flag absent)
findings.finding: The plan prescribes running every read surface — including `search` — with `--output json`, but the `search` subcommand does not accept a `--output`/`-o` flag: `_cmd_search` parses no output flag and rejects any `-`-prefixed arg outside its filter set with exit 2 (it always emits a JSON array by default). So `rebar search <query> --output json` exits 2, not JSON. Combined with the plan's rule that nonzero exits pass ('LOUD nonzero exit is acceptable' / assert-JSON only on exit 0), the search parameterization would exit 2 and pass VACUOUSLY, never exercising search's reconverge/output path — silently dropping the very surface the property exists to cover.
findings.location: Approach — 'Run every surface with `--output json`'; Acceptance Criteria line 1 (covers show/list/search/ready) & line 2 (exit-0-implies-JSON, nonzero passes)
scenarios: Parameterized test invokes `rebar search <q> --output json` → CLI returns exit 2 (usage error) → plan's 'nonzero exits pass' rule marks it green without ever asserting parseable output or exercising search's reconverge path
Author later relies on this suite to catch a search-surface reconverge regression; it never could, because search was never actually driven with a zero-exit read
findings.suggested_fix: In the surface parameterization, model each surface's real invocation rather than a blanket `--output json`: show/list/ready → append `--output json`; search → invoke bare (`rebar search <query>`), since it emits JSON unconditionally and rejects `--output` with exit 2. Assert the documented shape per surface (show=object; list/search/ready=array).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify the per-shape assertion: list surfaces assert stdout parses to a JSON list (empty `[]` allowed); `show` asserts stdout parses to a non-empty JSON object — either form fails json.loads on truncated/empty stdout.
evidence: Plan: 'exit 0 implies stdout parses as the surface's JSON shape (valid-empty `[]` passes; truncated/empty stdout fails)'
Plan also says the shape is 'list/object' — `show` is the object case, for which `[]` is not the empty form; the `[]` distinguishability argument does not cover it
findings.finding: The valid-empty rationale ('valid-empty serializes as `[]`, distinguishable from truncated-empty') only holds for list-shaped surfaces (list/search/ready); `show` returns a JSON object, never `[]`, so its truncation-detection assertion differs and is left implicit.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the invariant per surface shape: list surfaces => `isinstance(parsed, list)`; show => `isinstance(parsed, dict)` — both reject empty/truncated stdout via a failed parse.

findings.finding: The pinned invariant 'exit 0 implies non-empty output' is false for `rebar ready` in its default format: the `ready` output profile defaults to `text` (one ticket-id per line), so `rebar ready` with no unblocked tickets returns EMPTY stdout with exit 0 — legitimate behavior, not the ed2b bug — and the property would false-fail on that surface.
findings.location: Approach / Acceptance Criteria line 2 ('exit 0 implies non-empty parseable output')
findings.suggested_fix: Invoke each read surface with `--output json` in the parameterization and treat the invariant as 'exit 0 => stdout parses as JSON' (empty list `[]` is a valid non-empty parse); alternatively guarantee a non-empty ready set in the fixture.

findings.finding: The read-path reconverge is throttled to <=1/min via the /tmp/.ticket-sync-<md5> marker, so only the FIRST read in a 60s window actually reconverges and can stall on the held lock; every later read short-circuits to the local snapshot. The plan's storm loop runs well under 60s and does not mention clearing that throttle marker, so most parameterized reads never exercise the contended lock path — they assert only trivial non-emptiness, and the RED demonstration may not fire on every (or any) targeted surface.
findings.location: Approach ('under the same burst-of-writes contention ... every ZERO-exit read') / Testing (RED demonstration)
findings.suggested_fix: Hoist `_clear_sync_throttle` alongside the other helpers and call it before each read invocation (or set REBAR_SYNC_PULL such that reconverge is forced), then assert RED per-surface when the 2s ledge is reverted.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider the existing tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py concurrency suite (and its `_expire_sync_marker` throttle helper, line 75) as prior art: state why a new sibling module + hoisted `_clear_sync_throttle` is warranted over extending that suite, and factor the duplicated throttle-marker helper into ONE shared location rather than a third copy.
evidence: Plan: 'Generalize the existing ed2b harness rather than inventing a new storm' and 'bug-trend review change 20: one-time machinery, no bespoke per-surface copies'

test_concurrency_regression.py:75-91 `_expire_sync_marker` and test_show_no_stall.py:69-76 `_clear_sync_throttle` both unlink `/tmp/.ticket-sync-<md5(realpath(tracker))[:12]>` — the same helper duplicated
ed2b verification comment names test_concurrency_regression.py as adjacent concurrency machinery ('cover write-write concurrency and union reconvergence')
findings.finding: The plan frames its whole value as anti-duplication ('one-time machinery', 'no bespoke per-surface copies') and considers prior art ONLY within the ed2b sibling test_show_no_stall.py, but an established repo concurrency suite already exists — tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py, described as 'the executable form of the Concurrency Doctrine' — with a two-clone write-contention harness and a throttle-marker-expiry helper `_expire_sync_marker` (line 75) that computes the IDENTICAL `/tmp/.ticket-sync-<md5(realpath(tracker))[:12]>` marker as the `_clear_sync_throttle` helper (test_show_no_stall.py:69) the plan proposes to hoist. The plan neither cites nor reconciles against this existing suite/helper, so it risks landing a third copy of the throttle-clear helper and a parallel concurrency-property module.
findings.location: Approach / 'Throttle handling' paragraph; Scope (tests/interfaces/store/); AC 'ed2b harness reused (hoisted or imported), not duplicated'
scenarios: A reviewer asks why a new concurrency-property module lives under tests/interfaces/store/ instead of extending the existing tests/integration concurrency suite
The throttle-clear helper now exists in three places (two test files + the plan's hoist), each drifting independently
